# Concerning the Motion of the Heart, etc.

Since these things are so, it is certain that another point I previously stated will also be confirmed: namely, that the blood passes continually through the heart. For we see in the constitution of the body that the blood flows from the arteries into the veins, and not from the veins into the arteries. We see, moreover, that almost the entire mass of the blood can be drained from the arm itself <note>specifically through a single skin-deep vein opened with a scalpel, provided a proper ligature is applied</note>. We further observe that it is poured out so forcefully and abundantly that it is evident that not only the blood which was contained in the arm below the ligature before the incision is evacuated quickly and soon, but the blood from the whole arm and the whole body, from both the arteries and the veins.

Therefore, it must first be acknowledged that the blood is supplied with force and impulse, and is driven by force

<summary>Harvey demonstrates that blood flows in a one-way circuit from arteries to veins and can be entirely drained from a single incision due to continuous circulation. This evidence supports his theory that the heart acts as a pump driving the blood through the entire body.</summary>
